We normally use simple present tense to talk about food. Check out the following examples.
STATEMENTS
QUESTIONS
NEGATIVE STATEMENTS
1.
There is one apple on the table.
Is there one apple on the table?
There isn’t an apple on the table.
2.
There are a lot of eggs in the basket.
Are there a lot of eggs in the basket?
There aren’t any of eggs in the basket.
3.
I have some water in the bottle.
Do you have any water in the bottle?
I don’t have any water in the bottle.
To consider:
We use the expressions There is (singular) / there are (plural) to say something exists. 
We can use other verbs to talk about food. See example number 3. 
When we talk about food, we need to talk about quantity. We use containers and quantifiers: 
Some – Any – a lot of – Few / A few -  None – lots of – Much -  Many. 
Also, there are two main questions when we talk about quantities: 
How much – Used for uncountable nouns.  How much milk is there left?
How many – Used for countable nouns.  How many do you have?

texts: We normally use simple present tense to talk about food. Check out the following examples.
There is one apple on the table.
Is there one apple on the table?
There isn’t an apple on the table.
There are a lot of eggs in the basket.
Are there a lot of eggs in the basket?
There aren’t any of eggs in the basket.
I have some water in the bottle.
Do you have any water in the bottle?
I don’t have any water in the bottle.

To consider:
We use the expressions There is (singular) / there are (plural) to say something exists. 
We can use other verbs to talk about food. See example number 3. 
When we talk about food, we need to talk about quantity. We use containers and quantifiers: 
Some – Any – a lot of – Few / A few -  None – lots of – Much -  Many. 
Also, there are two main questions when we talk about quantities: 
How much – Used for uncountable nouns.  How much milk is there left?
How many – Used for countable nouns.  How many do you have?
